paragraphs: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. is a financial services holding company headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and one of the largest diversified financial institutions in the U.S. PNC has businesses engaged in retail banking, corporate and institutional banking and asset management, providing many of our products and services nationally. We are organized around our customers and communities for strong relationships and local delivery of retail and business banking including a full range of lending products; specialized services for corporations and government entities, including corporate banking, real estate finance and asset-based lending; wealth management and asset management. Our retail branch network is located coast-to-coast, and we also have strategic international offices in four countries outside the U.S. At December 31, 2025, our consolidated total assets, total deposits and total shareholders' equity were $573.6 billion, $440.9 billion and $60.6 billion, respectively.

We were incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania in 1983 with the consolidation of Pittsburgh National Corporation and Provident National Corporation. Since 1983, we have diversified our geographical presence, business mix and product capabilities through organic growth, strategic bank and non-bank acquisitions and equity investments, and the formation of various non-banking subsidiaries. We primarily conduct our business through our primary domestic bank subsidiary, PNC Bank, a national banking association chartered and located in Wilmington, Delaware. We offer a broad range of deposit, credit and fee-based products and services to serve our customers. Our non-banking subsidiaries engage in activities that are financial in nature, including market-making, securities underwriting, and advisory services and other permissible investment and merchant banking related activities. See Note 22 Segment Reporting for additional details regarding our business segments, products and services.

On January 5, 2026, PNC completed its acquisition of FirstBank Holding Company, including its banking subsidiary, FirstBank. As of close, FirstBank had $26.4 billion of assets, $16.0 billion of loans and $23.1 billion of deposits. Effective January 5, 2026, FirstBank's financial results are included in PNC's consolidated operations and will be reported in PNC's first quarter 2026 results. Conversion of FirstBank customers to PNC Bank is expected to occur this summer. Until conversion, FirstBank will remain a separate bank subsidiary of PNC. See Note 24 Subsequent Events for additional details on the acquisition of FirstBank.

Our corporate legal structure at December 31, 2025 consisted of one domestic bank subsidiary, including its subsidiaries, and 52 active non-bank subsidiaries, in addition to various affordable housing investments and historic rehabilitation investments. For additional information on certain of our subsidiaries, see Exhibit 21 to this Report.

The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc., is a BHC under the BHC Act that has elected to be an FHC under the GLB Act. We are subject to numerous governmental regulations, some of which are highlighted below. See Note 19 Regulatory Matters for additional information regarding our regulatory matters.

As a BHC, PNC is subject to regulation under the BHC Act and to comprehensive consolidated supervision, regulation and examination by its primary regulator, the Federal Reserve. PNC primarily conducts its business through its domestic bank subsidiary, PNC Bank, which is a national banking association chartered under the laws of the U.S. PNC Bank is supervised and regulated primarily by the OCC, and with respect to some matters, by the FDIC and the CFPB.

On January 5, 2026, PNC acquired FirstBank Holding Company and its bank subsidiary, FirstBank, a Colorado state-chartered bank. FirstBank is primarily regulated by the Federal Reserve and the Colorado Division of Banking. We expect to merge FirstBank into PNC Bank this summer. Until the merger, FirstBank will remain a separate bank subsidiary of PNC.

Comprehensive examinations by our many regulators consider not only compliance with applicable laws, regulations and supervisory policies of the agencies, but also capital levels, asset quality, risk management effectiveness, the ability and performance of management and the Board of Directors, the effectiveness of internal controls and internal audit function, earnings, liquidity and various other factors.

The federal bank regulators have broad supervisory and enforcement authority with regard to BHCs and banks, including the power to conduct examinations and investigations, which potentially can result in the imposition of significant limitations on our activities and growth. The federal bank regulators generally have broad discretion to impose restrictions and limitations on the operations of a regulated entity and take enforcement action against a regulated entity where the relevant agency determines, among other things, that the operations of the regulated entity or any of its subsidiaries fail to comply with applicable law or regulations, are conducted in an unsafe or unsound manner, or represent an unfair or deceptive act or practice. This supervisory framework, including the examination reports and supervisory ratings (which are not publicly available) of the agencies, could materially impact our operations.

The CFPB is responsible for examining us for compliance with most federal consumer financial protection laws, and the results of the CFPB's examinations (which are not publicly available) also can result in restrictions or limitations on our operations.

We also are subject to regulation by the SEC by virtue of our status as a public company and by the SEC and the CFTC due to the nature of some of our businesses. Our businesses with operations outside the U.S. also are subject to the laws and regulations of the foreign jurisdictions in which they do business.

The scope of the laws and regulations and the intensity of supervision to which we are subject are continually under review. New legislation, administration changes, changes in rules promulgated by federal bank regulators, other federal and state regulatory authorities and self-regulatory organizations, or rescissions, withdrawals, or changes in the interpretation, application, or enforcement of existing laws and rules may directly affect the operations and profitability of our businesses. The more detailed description of the significant regulations to which we are subject included in this Report is based on current laws and regulations and is subject to potential material change. For additional information on the impact of the regulatory environment on us and the financial services industry, see Item 1A Risk Factors in this Report.

There are numerous rules governing the regulation of financial services institutions and their holding companies. Accordingly, the following discussion is general in nature and does not purport to be complete or to describe all of the laws, regulations and policies that apply to us. The regulatory framework applicable to financial services institutions and their holding companies is not intended primarily to protect our shareholders and our non-customer creditors, but rather to protect our customers (including depositors), the DIF, the financial markets, and the U.S. banking and financial system in general.

Regulatory Capital Requirements. PNC and PNC Bank are subject to the regulatory capital requirements under the U.S. Basel III capital rules adopted by the Federal Reserve, for PNC, and by the OCC, for the Bank. The regulatory capital rules establish minimum requirements for the ratios of a banking organization's regulatory capital to its risk-weighted assets, referred to as risk-based capital requirements, as well as for the ratios of its regulatory capital to measures of assets and other exposures, referred to as leverage capital requirements.

paragraphs: We are subject to a number of risks potentially impacting our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. As a financial services company, certain elements of risk are inherent in what we do and the business decisions we make. Thus, we encounter risk as part of the normal course of our business, and we design risk management processes to help manage these risks. For more information about how we manage risks, see the Risk Management section in Item 7 of this Report.

The following are the material risk factors that affect us of which we are currently aware. Any one or more of these risk factors could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows. In addition, these risks present other possible adverse consequences, including those described below. These risk factors and other risks we face are also discussed further in other sections of this Report. Thus, the risk factors below should not be considered a complete list of potential risks that we may face.

Our business and overall financial performance are affected to a significant extent by economic conditions, primarily in the U.S. Declining or adverse economic conditions and adverse changes in investor, consumer and business sentiment generally result in reduced business activity, which may decrease the demand for our products and services or reduce the number of creditworthy borrowers. The ability of borrowers to repay loans is often weakened as a result of economic downturns, higher inflation and unemployment. In addition, adverse economic conditions may limit the availability of, or increase the costs of, capital and labor, erode customer purchasing power, confidence and spending and may also reduce our tolerance for extending credit. Increases in costs or expenses impacting our customers' operations and financial performance, such as the interest rates payable on their debt obligations, could increase our credit risk or decrease the demand for our products and services.

We operate in an uncertain economic environment due to sustained inflationary pressures, including higher prices and lower housing affordability, and fluctuating trade policies (including tariffs), combined with geopolitical tensions. These conditions have led and may continue to lead to turmoil and volatility in financial markets, often with at least some financial asset categories losing value. Financial market volatility could also result from uncertainty about the timing and extent of rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. Any of these effects would likely have an adverse impact on our operations and financial performance, with the significance of the impact generally

depending on the nature and severity of the adverse economic conditions. Even when economic conditions are relatively good or stable, specific economic factors can negatively affect our business and performance. This can be especially true when the factors relate to particular segments of the economy and impact our customers whose operations or financial conditions directly or indirectly depend on good or stable conditions in those segments. For example, underutilization of commercial real estate space, combined with higher interest rates, has harmed some customers' creditworthiness and ability to refinance maturing loans, and decreased the demand for financial services in that sector.

Our foreign business activities and operations continue to be a relatively small part of our overall business. As a result, the direct impact on our business and financial performance from economic conditions outside the U.S. is not likely to be significant, although the impact would increase if we expanded our foreign business and operations more than nominally. We are, however, susceptible to the risk that foreign economic conditions, trade policies (including tariffs) and geopolitical tensions could negatively affect our business and financial performance. Primarily, this risk results from the possibility that poor economic conditions or financial market disruptions affecting other major economies would also affect the U.S.

paragraphs: Statements regarding our business outlook are forward-looking within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Our forward-looking financial statements are subject, among other things, to the risk that economic and financial market conditions will be substantially different than those we are currently expecting and do not take into account potential legal and regulatory contingencies. These statements are based on our views that:

•PNC's baseline forecast remains for continued expansion, but slower economic growth in 2026 than in 2024 and 2025. Tariffs remain a drag on consumer spending and business investment, while AI-related capex and wealth effects have been key supports to growth. Consumer spending growth is slowing to a pace more consistent with household income growth. The One Big Beautiful Bill will be a net positive for economic growth in 2026.

•The baseline forecast anticipates real GDP growth slowing to around 2% in 2026, with continued modest job gains and the unemployment rate at around 4.5%. Tariffs remain a risk to the outlook, and a reversal in sentiment around AI or a large decline in equity prices would be drags. Weaker labor force growth could lead to weaker long-run growth.

•Our baseline forecast is for the Federal Reserve to keep the federal funds rate unchanged in the first half of this year, in a range between 3.50% and 3.75%. We expect modest additional easing in the second half of the year with 25 basis points cuts at the FOMC meetings in July and September 2026, resulting in a federal funds rate in the range of 3.00% to 3.25% by the fall. However, there are two-sided risks to this outlook: (1) if inflation re-accelerates or proves more persistent than expected, the Federal Reserve may cut less or (2) if growth falters or recession emerges, easing could be deeper and more prolonged.

See Item 1A Risk Factors and the Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Information section in this Item 7 for other factors that could cause future events to differ, perhaps materially, from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements.

paragraphs: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. 為一間財務服務控股公司，總部設於賓夕法尼亞州匹茲堡，為美國最大的多元化財務機構之一。PNC 有業務涉及零售銀行、企業及機構銀行與資產管理，提供許多產品與服務於全美各地。我們以客戶與社區為中心，建立強大的關係與在地化零售與企業銀行服務，包括完整的貸款產品；針對企業與政府機構的專業服務，包括企業銀行、不動產融資與以資產為基礎的貸款；資產管理與財富管理。我們的零售分行網路橫跨全美，我們也在美國以外的四個國家設有戰略性國際辦事處。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們合併總資產、總存款與總股東權益分別為 5736 億美元、4409 億美元與 606 億美元。

我們於 1983 年根據賓夕法尼亞州法律成立，為 Pittsburgh National Corporation 與 Provident National Corporation 合併後的公司。自 1983 年以來，我們透過內生成長、戰略銀行與非銀行收購與股權投資，以及設立各種非銀行子公司，擴大了我們的地理分佈、業務組合與產品能力。我們主要透過我們的主要國內銀行子公司 PNC Bank 進行業務，PNC Bank 為一間根據美國法律設立的全國性銀行協會，位於特拉華州威明頓。我們提供廣泛的存款、信貸與收費型產品與服務，以服務客戶。我們的非銀行子公司從事具有金融性質的活動，包括市場做市、證券經紀與顧問服務及其他允許的投資與商人銀行相關活動。有關我們業務分部、產品與服務的更多細節，請參閱第 22 註腳「分部報告」。

2026 年 1 月 5 日，PNC 完成對 FirstBank Holding Company 的收購，包括其銀行子公司 FirstBank。截至收購日，FirstBank 的資產為 264 億美元，貸款為 160 億美元，存款為 231 億美元。自 2026 年 1 月 5 日起，FirstBank 的財務結果已納入 PNC 的合併營運，並將在 PNC 的 2026 年第一季財務報告中披露。FirstBank 客戶轉換至 PNC Bank 預計將於本年夏天進行。轉換前，FirstBank 將繼續作為 PNC 的獨立銀行子公司。有關收購 FirstBank 的更多細節，請參閱第 24 註腳「後續事件」。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的企業法律結構包含一間國內銀行子公司及其子公司，以及 52 間活躍的非銀行子公司，加上各種可負擔住宅投資與歷史復原投資。有關某些子公司的更多資訊，請參閱本報告的附錄 21。
PNC Financial Services Group, Inc. 為一間根據《銀行控股公司法》設立的銀行控股公司，並已選擇成為根據《葛拉姆-李德法案》設立的金融控股公司。我們受多項政府規範管制，部分重點如下。有關我們的規範事項，請參閱第 19 註腳「規範事項」。
作為一間銀行控股公司，PNC 受《銀行控股公司法》規範，並受其主要監管機構美國聯邦儲備局的全面合併監督、規範與檢查。PNC 主要透過其國內銀行子公司 PNC Bank 進行業務，PNC Bank 為一間根據美國法律設立的全國性銀行協會。PNC Bank 主要受美國國稅局監督與規範，並在某些事項上受美國存款保險公司與美國消費者金融保護局監督。
2026 年 1 月 5 日，PNC 收購了 FirstBank Holding Company 及其銀行子公司 FirstBank，一間科羅拉多州註冊的銀行。FirstBank 主要受美國聯邦儲備局與科羅拉多州銀行管理局監督。我們預計將於本年夏天將 FirstBank 合併至 PNC Bank。在合併前，FirstBank 將繼續作為 PNC 的獨立銀行子公司。
我們的多項監管機構進行的全面檢查，不僅考量是否符合各機構的相關法律、規範與監督政策，也考量資本水平、資產質量、風險管理成效、管理層與董事會的能力建構與表現、內部控制與內部稽核功能的成效、營收、流動性以及各種其他因素。

美國聯邦銀行監管機構對銀行控股公司及銀行擁有廣泛的監督與執行權限，包括進行檢查與調查的權力，這可能會導致對我們的業務活動與成長施加重大限制。美國聯邦銀行監管機構通常對受監管機構的運作擁有廣泛的裁量權，並可對受監管機構採取執行行動，若相關機構認為，受監管機構或其任何子公司之運作未符合適用法律或規則、以不安全或不健全方式進行，或代表不公或欺詐行為。此監督架構，包括監管機構的檢查報告與監督評級（這些資訊並未公開），可能會對我們的業務運作產生重大影響。
消費者金融保護局（CFPB）負責檢查我們是否符合大多數聯邦消費者金融保護法律，且CFPB的檢查結果（這些資訊並未公開）也可能導致對我們的業務運作施加限制或限制。
我們也因為是上市公司而受美國證券交易委員會（SEC）的監管，並因部分業務性質而受SEC與商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）的監管。我們在美國境外運作的業務也受其營運國家的法律與規則所規範。

我們所受法律與規則的範圍與監督強度持續受到審查。新立法、行政變更、聯邦銀行監管機構所頒布規則的變更，或其他聯邦與州級監管機構與自律組織的變更，或現有法律與規則的廢止、撤回或解釋、適用或執行方式的變更，可能會直接影響我們業務的運作與獲利能力。本報告中更詳細說明我們所受重大規範的描述，基於現行法律與規則，並可能受到重大變更的影響。如需瞭解監管環境對我們與金融服務產業的影響，請參閱本報告第1A項風險因素。
有許多規則規範金融服務機構及其控股公司的監管。因此，以下討論為一般性質，並未試圖完整說明適用於我們的所有法律、規則與政策。適用於金融服務機構及其控股公司的監管架構，主要目的並非保護我們的股東與非客戶債權人，而是保護我們的客戶（包括存款人）、存款保險基金（DIF）、金融市場以及美國的銀行與金融體系。
監管資本要求。PNC與PNC Bank受美國巴塞爾III資本規則的監管資本要求所規範，該規則由聯邦儲備系統（Federal Reserve）針對PNC，以及由美國國有銀行與儲蓄機構管理局（OCC）針對PNC Bank所採用。監管資本規則設定了銀行機構的監管資本與風險加權資產比率的最低要求，稱為風險基礎資本要求，以及監管資本與資產及其他 exposures 測量值的比率，稱為槓桿資本要求。

paragraphs: 本公司對營業展望之說明係依照1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案之定義屬前瞻性陳述。本公司之前瞻性財務資料受多種因素影響，包括經濟與財務市場條件可能與本公司目前預期有顯著差異，且未考量潛在之法律與監管相關事項。這些說明係基於本公司之觀點：
•PNC之基準預測仍維持持續擴張，但2026年經濟成長速度將較2024年與2025年為慢。關稅仍對消費者支出與企業投資造成負面影響，而與AI相關之資本支出與財富效應則為成長之主要支撐。消費者支出成長速度將放緩，與家庭收入成長速度較為一致。One Big Beautiful Bill將為2026年經濟成長帶來淨正面影響。
•基準預測預期實質GDP成長速度將降至約2%，並持續有溫和就業增加，失業率將維持在約4.5%。關稅仍為展望之風險，若對AI之觀感出現逆轉或股市價格大幅下跌，將為負面因素。勞動力成長較弱可能導致長期成長較弱。

•本公司基準預測為聯邦儲備理事會在本年度上半年維持聯邦基金利率不變，維持在3.50%至3.75%之間。我們預期在本年度下半年有溫和進一步寬鬆，於2026年7月與9月聯邦公開市場委員會會議中各降25個基點，使聯邦基金利率在秋季維持在3.00%至3.25%之間。然而，此展望存在雙面風險：(1) 若通貨膨脹重新加速或比預期更持久，聯邦儲備理事會可能減幅較小，或(2) 若經濟成長受阻或出現衰退，寬鬆措施可能更為深遠且持續。
請參閱本項目第1A項風險因素及有關前瞻性資訊之警示聲明部分，以瞭解其他可能導致未來事件與這些前瞻性說明預期有顯著差異的因素。
2026年全年與2025年全年比較，本公司預期：•平均貸款將增加約8% ，
•淨利息收入將增加約14% ，•非利息收入將增加約6% ，
•非利息費用（扣除一次性整合費用）將增加約7% ，且
•預期稅率約為 19.5%。
2026 年第一季，相較於 2025 年第四季，我們預期：•平均貸款餘額將增加約 5% ，
•淨利息收入將增加約 6% ，•手續費收入將減少 1% 到 2% ，•其他非利息收入將在 1.5 億美元至 2 億美元之間，
•營業收入將增加 2% 到 3% ，•非利息費用（排除一次性整合成本）將增加約 4% ，
•淨貸款違約損失將約為 2 億美元，

paragraphs: 本公司面臨許多可能影響我們業務、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流的風險。作為一家金屬服務公司，我們的業務中某些風險是內在的，且與我們所做的商業決策有關。因此，我們在業務的正常運作中會遇到風險，並設計風險管理程序來協助管理這些風險。如需瞭解我們如何管理風險，請參閱本報告第7項的風險管理部分。
以下為目前我們所知的影響我們的重大風險因素。任何一個或數個風險因素都可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果或現金流造成重大不利影響。此外，這些風險可能帶來其他可能的不利後果，包括以下所描述的。這些風險因素及其他我們面臨的風險，也在本報告的其他部分進一步討論。因此，以下的風險因素不應被視為我們可能面臨的全部潛在風險清單。

我們的業務與整體財務表現受到經濟條件的重大影響，尤其是美國的經濟條件。經濟衰退或不利的經濟條件，以及投資者、消費者與企業情緒的惡化，通常會導致商業活動減少，這可能會降低對我們產品與服務的需求，或減少信用良好的借款人數量。借款人償還貸款的能力往往會因經濟衰退、通貨膨脹與失業率上升而受到削弱。此外，不利的經濟條件可能會限制資本與勞動力的可取得性，或提高其成本，削弱客戶的購買力、信心與消費支出，也可能降低我們對延長信貸的容忍度。影響客戶營運與財務表現的成本或費用增加，例如他們債務義務的利率支出，可能會增加我們的信貸風險，或降低對我們產品與服務的需求。
我們處於一個不確定的經濟環境中，這是因為持續的通貨膨脹壓力，包括價格上漲與住宅負擔能力下降，以及波動的貿易政策（包括關稅），加上地緣政治緊張局勢。這些條件已導致並可能繼續導致財務市場的動盪與波動，通常至少某些財務資產類別會失去價值。財務市場的波動也可能來自對聯邦儲備委員會降息時間與幅度的不確定性。任何這些影響都可能對我們的營運與財務表現造成不利影響，影響的程度通常
取決於不利經濟條件的性質與嚴重程度。即使經濟條件相對良好或穩定，特定經濟因素仍可能對我們的業務與表現造成負面影響。這一點在這些因素與特定經濟部門相關，並影響到我們客戶的營運或財務狀況直接或間接依賴這些部門的良好或穩定條件時，尤其顯得重要。例如，商業不動產空間利用率不足，加上利率上升，已對某些客戶的信用worthiness與重組到期貸款的能力造成傷害，並降低該領域對金融服務的需求。
我們的海外業務活動與營運目前仍是我們整體業務相對較小的一部分。因此，來自美國以外經濟條件對我們業務與財務表現的直接影響，不太可能顯著。不過，如果我們擴大海外業務與營運的程度超過一般水平，這種影響將會增加。然而，我們仍然面臨海外經濟條件、貿易政策（包括關稅）與地緣政治緊張局勢可能對我們業務與財務表現造成負面影響的風險。主要原因是，其他主要經濟體的不良經濟條件或財務市場動盪可能也會影響美國。
